title: agda-deps v2 graph.json (expanded mode)
description: Wire schema for the JSON that `agda-deps --format=json --json-mode=expanded` emits. The field tables and encoder in `AgdaDeps.Backend.Wire` are the single source of truth; this committed schema is generated to match them, and CI validates freshly-generated expanded output against it. `required` lists the fields the producer has emitted since v2 inception; fields declared additive in `AgdaDeps.Backend.Wire` are optional, so this schema validates both current and older v2 output. `additionalProperties` is `true` throughout: downstream readers ignore unknown fields, and a future additive field must not fail v2 validation. The `packed` mode (CSR + base64 typed arrays) and the `--lazy` split-file layout are NOT covered here.

v.description: Wire-shape version. A consumer must refuse a `v` it doesn't recognise.

schemaVersion.description: Expanded-form schema version (mirrors `v` for the expanded shape).

nodeKeyVersion.description: Additive. Node-naming convention version (orthogonal to the schema version). Absent in older JSON, where a reader assumes 1. Lets a downstream reader spot a stale-format cache.

producer.description: Additive. Build fingerprint of the emitting agda-deps, e.g. "agda-deps 1.1 (git <sha>+, built <date>, ghc 9.14)".

modules.description: All module names referenced in the graph (definitions' modules, import-edge endpoints, the entry, failed and extra modules).

entryModule.description: The IsMain entry module, or null when unknown.

externalModules.description: Modules classified as external (outside the project root).

failedModules.description: Modules whose type-check raised under --keep-going (each gets an `F`-state marker node).

definitionEdges.description: Leaf dependency edges as [sourceName, targetName] pairs, keyed by `definition.name`.

definitionEdgesProvenance.description: Additive (round 4). Parallel to `definitionEdges`: index i tags how edge i was discovered. When present, MUST be the same length as `definitionEdges` (a cross-array invariant this schema cannot express; the consumer enforces it). Absent in older JSON, where every edge is treated as "unknown".

moduleEdges.description: Module-level edges as [sourceModule, targetModule] pairs (leaf edges lifted to modules, unioned with import edges).

transitiveModuleEdges.description: Transitive closure of `moduleEdges` as [sourceModule, targetModule] pairs.

moduleFiles.description: Map from module name to its source file path.

sourceFiles.description: Source file paths discovered by the scan.

reexports.description: Public re-export rows (`open import M public`).

moduleOptionEscapes.description: Optional (R15). Per module, the file-level `{-# OPTIONS #-}` soundness escapes (`--type-in-type`, `--no-positivity-check`, `--rewriting`, …) that make `agda --safe` reject it. Only modules with at least one escape appear; omitted entirely when none does, so escape-free corpora stay byte-identical. Module-level, orthogonal to per-def `unsafe`. Per-block declaration pragmas (`{-# NO_POSITIVITY_CHECK #-}`) are NOT OPTIONS pragmas and never appear here.

moduleEffectiveOptions.description: Optional. Per module, the actionability-relevant Agda options actually IN FORCE — currently `--erasure` only. Read from the interface's EFFECTIVE options, so unlike `moduleOptionEscapes` (deliberately the file's own `{-# OPTIONS #-}` tokens) it covers the `.agda-lib` `flags:` line and the command line, which is where such a flag normally lives. Only modules enabling one appear; omitted entirely when none does. Use it to gate advice: without `--erasure`, `@0` is a syntax error (`[AttributeKindNotEnabled]`), so every `argUsage.erasable` verdict in that module is un-appliable as configured however true it is.

unsolvedModules.description: Optional (--allow-unsolved-metas / --lenient-imports). Per top-level module, the source lines of SILENT unsolved metavariables (missing record fields, failed instance search, unsolved `_` — what plain `agda` reports as UnsolvedMetaVariables) and of unsolved constraints. Honest interaction `?` holes are NOT listed — they surface only as per-def state `H`. Only modules with at least one entry appear; omitted entirely when none does. Under these flags such modules 'succeeded' with un-produced evidence, so an empty `failedModules` alone must not be read as 'everything compiles'.

definitionSubtermHashes.description: Additive (round 6, --with-term-hashes). Parallel to `definitions`: index i is that def's array of canonical-subterm Word64 fingerprints (emitted as JSON numbers). When present, MUST be the same length as `definitions`.

definitionSubtermDepths.description: Additive (round 6, --with-term-hashes). Parallel to `definitionSubtermHashes`: the AST depth of each emitted subterm. Same length contract.

externals_summary.description: Additive (--no-externals). Diagnostic record of the externals stripped from the graph; absent otherwise.

edge.description: A directed edge encoded as a two-element [source, target] array of wire names.

state.description: Definition lifecycle: Defined / Postulate / Hole / Failed.

kind.description: Structural kind. `other` covers external library references with no local definition.

access.description: Defining-module visibility. Absent in the JSON means `public`.

provenance.description: How an edge was discovered: defType (signature), theDef body, anonymous-module-local helper (where-block helper or parameterised-section member; does not imply ownership by this source), or unclassified. A `with` value existed through 2026-08-31 and was removed as unreachable: `funWith` names a with-function's parent and is non-empty on exactly the definitions the node filter drops, so no corpus could ever produce the tag. A dependency reached only through a `with`-abstraction arrives on the parent as `body` (the with-helper's edges are contracted into it), which post-elaboration is indistinguishable from any other body reference.

unsafeTag.description: A soundness escape a definition uses directly: `non-terminating` (a `{-# NON_TERMINATING #-}` function) or `trustme` (the body/type references `primTrustMe`). A `{-# TERMINATING #-}` marker is deliberately NOT surfaced: Agda's ordinary termination checker also stamps proven defs, so it cannot be distinguished from a normal proof.

hiding.description: How a binder is written, hence how a call site passes it: `explicit` (`(x : A)` / `A`), `implicit` (`{x : A}`) or `instance` (`⦃ x : A ⦄`).

name.description: Additive/optional. The binder name as Agda spells it. Omitted when the spine binds no name (`Nat → Nat`), so absence means "unnamed", not "unknown". A name containing a `.` (e.g. `P.A`) is NOT a source binder: it is one Agda inserted by generalising a `variable` declaration (a dependency of the variable the signature mentions), and since a written binder name can never contain `.`, that is a sound test for "this position has no binder on the signature line to edit". Reported as-is because it is the name Agda's own printer uses — the sibling `type` string shows it too.

type.description: Additive/optional (--with-signatures). This binder's domain, reified to one line in the context of the binders before it — the slice of the signature at THIS position, which the sibling per-def `type` string cannot provide because it is not re-indexed onto the definition's own binders. Present only under `--with-signatures`; absence there means the flag was off, not that the binder has no type. Reified internal syntax, not source text: implicit and instance arguments Agda solved are printed as it prints them, and `--show-implicit` makes that more verbose. Never normalised (`--normalise-signatures` governs the per-def `type` only), because reducing a domain destroys the head symbol that makes it recognisable. This is what names a binder in a proof development, where premises are routinely written unnamed.

argBinder.description: One reported argument as written: its hiding, its name when it has one, and its type under --with-signatures.

metas.description: 1-based source lines of silent unsolved metas, ascending — one entry per meta (exact: derived from the `unsolved#meta.*` markers / live meta store, not from highlighting spans).

constraints.description: 1-based source lines flagged as opening an unsolved constraint, ascending and deduplicated (best-effort: derived from highlighting spans, so adjacent constraints on one line collapse).

removable.description: Telescope positions (0-based, implicits included, ascending) whose binder AND corresponding argument at every call site can be deleted. Interprocedural — an argument threaded into a helper that discards it counts as unused here too. Agda's `Unused` + `Nonvariant` verdict is necessary but not sufficient, and is filtered: a position whose variable still occurs in the rest of the type (the codomain, or the domain of a later argument that is not itself being removed) is NOT reported, even though Agda calls it unused. That filter is what makes this field mean deletability rather than "the meaning does not depend on this value" — an argument occurring only at an IRRELEVANT position (`.(p : A)`, or a relevant binder handed to a callee that consumes it irrelevantly) is invisible to Agda's own relevance-aware occurrence test, so without the filter such a binder looks removable and deleting it leaves the type naming something out of scope.

removableRequires.description: Additive/optional. Positions that cannot be removed on their own: maps a `removable` position (as a decimal string key) to the other `removable` positions that must be deleted along with it, transitively and ascending. A position absent from this map — and the whole map, absent whenever every removal stands alone, which includes every single-entry `removable` — can be removed by itself. Requirements always point FORWARD (every value is greater than its key), since the only thing that can still mention a removable binder's variable is the domain of a later removable argument. Example: `{"0": [1, 3]}` on `removable: [0,1,3]` means deleting 0 also forces 1 and 3, while 1 and 3 each stand alone.

occursInBody.description: Additive/optional. The subset of `removable` whose variable the ELABORATED BODY still mentions — the value is passed on to a callee that discards it, so the deletion is a multi-definition edit rather than a local one (the callee's parameter and every call site have to go too). A `removable` position ABSENT from this array is a local edit: strike the binder and the arguments, nothing else changes. Omitted when no position qualifies, so absence reads as "all local". The instance case is worth calling out: an instance argument that never appears syntactically in the source body but which INSTANCE SEARCH resolves from is a body occurrence here, and is exactly the shape that makes a removal break a call — filter on it together with `binders[i].hiding == "instance"`. Conservative: a position matched on (a constructor or literal pattern), a position in a copattern clause, and a position past the clause's patterns are all reported as occurring.

erasable.description: Telescope positions that are `Unused` but NOT `Nonvariant`: used only in types, so a later binder or the codomain depends on them. An `@0` (run-time-erasure) candidate, NOT a removal — deleting one of these breaks the signature.

arity.description: Number of telescope positions the verdict ranges over; every index in either array is `< arity`. THE INDEX SPACE IS THE DEFINITION'S OWN *REDUCED* TELESCOPE — elaborated, with any inherited section telescope subtracted — and it MAY EXCEED THE SIGNATURE LINE, because Agda derives the underlying analysis from a reduced spine: a type whose codomain only becomes a function after unfolding a definition (`f : (A : Set) → Tracer A` with `Tracer A = ⋯ → ⋯ → A → A`) contributes positions with no written binder at all. Do not read these indices against the sibling `type` string, and do not assume `arity` counts binders on the source line — use `syntacticArity` for that boundary.

syntacticArity.description: Additive/optional. How many of the `arity` positions are ON THE SIGNATURE LINE: the length of the definition's syntactic `Pi` spine, section prefix subtracted. Always `<= arity`; OMITTED when the two are equal, so absence means "every position is a written binder". A position `>= syntacticArity` exists only after a type in the signature is unfolded and has no binder to strike out — but it is still a real finding worth reporting ("the proof never inspects this hypothesis", i.e. the statement could be strengthened), so it is labelled rather than dropped. This is the same boundary an absent `binders` entry marks, stated as a number: `binders` keys are always `< syntacticArity`.

partiallyApplied.description: Additive/optional. `true` when this definition is referenced somewhere IN THIS GRAPH with fewer arguments than it takes — used as a value rather than fully applied (`EagerlyAfterT t = Eager ∩¹ AfterT t` needs `AfterT t` to be a unary predicate). Its arity is then part of its interface and NO position is really removable, however dead the polarity analysis finds it. Omitted when false. Corpus-scoped, so it is only as complete as the modules compiled: an unsaturated reference from a module outside the graph cannot be seen. Measured on `Def` heads only — constructor applications carry no data parameters in their elaborated spine and would all look partial.

binders.description: Additive/optional. How the reported positions are *written*, so a report line can say `argument 0 ({A : Set})` instead of `argument 0`. Keyed like `removableRequires` (position as a decimal string) and SPARSE: only positions listed in `removable` or `erasable`, and only those the definition's syntactic `Pi` spine reaches — equivalently, only positions `< syntacticArity`. An absent position carries NO information — it is not a claim that the binder is explicit or unnamed; it means the position is past the signature line. A PRESENT entry with no `name` is a binder that IS written, spelled `_`. Absent entirely when no reported position has an entry (a definition whose type only becomes a function after unfolding). Read against the definition's own source signature line, never against the sibling `type` string: like the index arrays, these are re-indexed past any inherited section telescope.

argUsage.description: One definition's never-used-argument verdict. INDICES ARE THE DEFINITION'S OWN REDUCED TELESCOPE (section prefix subtracted) and may exceed the signature line — see `arity` and `syntacticArity`.

id.description: Index into `definitions` (sorted by node-key hash). -1 for references with no local definition.

name.description: Canonical wire name (`nodeKey`): prettyShow plus an @<binding-line> suffix for `._.` helpers. Edge endpoints key on this.

line.description: Additive/optional. 1-based start line; absent when the producer didn't know.

type.description: Additive/optional (--with-signatures). Reified type signature, as-written (not normalised), collapsed to one line.

unsafe.description: Additive/optional (R12). Soundness escapes this definition uses DIRECTLY (not transitively). Always computed (no flag); omitted when empty, so escape-free defs stay byte-identical. Orthogonal to `state`: a def can be `D` and still carry escapes.

unsolvedMetas.description: Additive/optional. Count of SILENT unsolved metavariables this definition mentions directly (non-interaction open metas: missing record fields, failed instance search, unsolved `_`). Honest interaction `?` holes are NOT counted — they only set `state` to `H`. So `H` with no `unsolvedMetas` = honest open goal(s) only; `H` with `unsolvedMetas` = silently-missing evidence. Always computed (no flag); omitted when 0.

argUsage.description: Additive/optional. Arguments this definition never actually uses, read off the positivity/polarity analysis Agda already runs for every mutual block. Always computed (no flag); the whole object is omitted when there is nothing to report, so finding-free corpora stay byte-identical. Indices are over the definition's OWN binders — Agda prepends the enclosing section's telescope to every definition inside it, and those inherited positions are dropped, so a `where` helper's indices line up with its own signature line rather than the lifted one. CAUTION: this means the indices are NOT positions in the sibling `type` string, which reifies the raw elaborated telescope and therefore still shows the section-inherited binders (e.g. a def in `module M (k : Nat)` renders as `(k : Nat) -> ...` while its `argUsage.arity` counts only its own binders). Align indices against the definition's source signature, never against `type`. Only non-projection-like functions are analysed: projections and constructors drop parameters from the underlying lists (so their indices would be shifted), and for datatypes/records `Nonvariant` parameters are deliberately purged to allow phantom types.

x.description: Layout x position, or null when no layout was computed.

y.description: Layout y position, or null when no layout was computed.

from.description: Host module doing `open import M public`.

renames.description: Additive/optional (R14). Map from each `renaming`d in-scope alias to the canonical `nodeKey` it resolves to (a member of `names`). Omitted when the row has no renamed entries, so rename-free corpora stay byte-identical.

postulates_by_module.description: Per dropped module, the unqualified postulate names it held.
